defaults.permitted_development: A single-storey ground floor extension can be permitted development in Scotland outside conservation areas where it remains to the rear or other non-road-facing part of the house and stays within the height, depth and boundary limits.

rules.height_rules: Eaves should not exceed 3m and overall height should not exceed 4m. Any part within 1m of the boundary should not be higher than 2.5m.
rules.depth_rules: A rear projection should not exceed 3m on a terraced house or 4m on any other house.
rules.boundary_rules: The extension should not be forward of the principal elevation or a side elevation that fronts a road. It should also stay within the normal curtilage limits used for householder permitted development.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof subordinate to the house and avoid using a roof form that pushes the extension above what Scottish householder PDR will tolerate at the boundary or on a prominent elevation.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials and detailing that sit appropriately with the existing house.
